summary: This is a clipped Snowflake documentation page for the DROP PIPE command, which removes a specified pipe from the current or specified schema. It gives the syntax (DROP PIPE [ IF EXISTS ] <name>), explains the name parameter and its quoting and case-sensitivity rules, notes that dropped pipes cannot be recovered, and shows an example that drops a pipe named mypipe. Navigation and footer boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the DROP PIPE command, which permanently removes a named pipe from a schema.
key_facts: DROP PIPE removes the specified pipe from the current or specified schema.
The syntax is DROP PIPE [ IF EXISTS ] <name>.
The name parameter specifies the identifier for the pipe to drop.
If a pipe identifier contains spaces or special characters, the entire string must be enclosed in double quotes.
Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are case-sensitive.
Dropped pipes cannot be recovered and must be recreated.
The example DROP PIPE mypipe; returns the status 'MYPIPE successfully dropped.'
